steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is typically 6 hours ahead of U.S. Eastern Time in September (ET = EDT, UTC−4; Madrid = CEST, UTC+2). So 5:00 PM ET on September 30, 2026 is 11:00 PM in Madrid on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is on PET (UTC−5) year-round, so the deadline at 12:00 UTC is 5 hours earlier locally.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST is 7 hours behind Tokyo time (JST), so add 7 hours to the deadline.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on CEST on October 11, 2026, which is 9 hours ahead of PDT. So the deadline is the next day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST on March 3, 2026 is UTC−8. Madrid on that date is on CET (UTC+1), which is 9 hours ahead of PST.

So the deadline is on the next day in Madrid:

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Los Angeles will be on Pacific Time in February 2026 (PST, UTC−8). CET on February 2, 2026 is UTC+1, so the deadline is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles time.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is on PET (UTC-5), and Japan Standard Time is JST (UTC+9), so Lima is 14 hours behind JST.

8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026 converts to 6:00 PM in Lima on May 4, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Time in late October, but by October 28, 2026 Spain will be on CET/CEST? Let’s convert from PT first:

- PT on October 28, 2026 is Pacific Daylight Time (UTC−7), since Pacific time switches back in early November.
- 11:59 PM PT = 06:59 UTC on October 29, 2026.
- Madrid will be on Central European Time? By October 29, 2026, Spain has already left daylight saving time, so it is CET (UTC+1).

So the deadline in Madrid is 07:59 on October 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Time/Daylight Time, while ET on October 30, 2026 is Eastern Daylight Time (UTC−4). Madrid will be 6 hours ahead, so 9:00 AM ET is 3:00 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 15:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is 6 hours ahead of New York local time during late October 2026 if New York is on daylight saving time (EDT), so subtract 6 hours from 18:00 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 12:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on CET/CEST, while PT on November 2, 2026 is Pacific Standard Time (UTC−8) because daylight saving has already ended in the U.S. By then, Madrid is on Central European Time (UTC+1), which is 9 hours ahead of PT.

So 11:59 PM PT on November 2, 2026 becomes 8:59 AM in Madrid on November 3, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on CET/CEST, and on March 20, 2026 Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1), while PT is UTC-7 at that date. So the deadline is 8 hours ahead in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET on March 25, 2026 is UTC+1, and Los Angeles is on PDT (UTC-7) then, so the local time is 8 hours earlier.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026” means midnight at the start of October 12 in U.S. Eastern Time.

Madrid will be 6 hours ahead of ET on that date (EDT), so the local deadline is:

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“23:59 AoE” means 23:59 in the AoE time zone (UTC−12).  
Madrid is on CEST in early October 2026 (UTC+2), so Madrid is 14 hours ahead of AoE.

So the deadline in Madrid local time is:

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in Spain, which is typically 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time in mid-August (PT is PDT then). So 12:00 PM PT on August 14, 2026 is 21:00 in Madrid on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST is UTC+5:30, and Madrid is on CET in November (UTC+1), so Madrid is 4 hours 30 minutes behind IST.

So, 11:59 PM IST on November 10, 2026 = 7:29 PM in Madrid on November 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is on PET (UTC−5). Nepal time is NPT (UTC+5:45), so Nepal is 10 hours 45 minutes ahead of Lima.

So 5:00 PM on April 2, 2026 in Nepal is 4:15 AM on April 2, 2026 in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 04:15 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide is on daylight saving time on October 6, 2026 (ACDT, UTC+10:30), while Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). That makes Adelaide 8 hours 30 minutes ahead of Madrid.

So 10:00 AM in Adelaide is 1:30 AM in Madrid on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney will be on daylight saving time then (AEDT, UTC+11), while Madrid will be on CEST (UTC+2) on that date. So the deadline is 9 hours earlier in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 09:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).
